title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

summary.tldr: Design patterns are proven, reusable solutions to common software design problems organized into three categories (Creational, Structural, Behavioral) and grounded in SOLID principles. They improve code reusability, communication, and maintainability but require careful application to avoid over-engineering.
key_insights: Design patterns provide tested, proven solutions to recurring problems
Patterns should solve real problems, not be applied blindly
SOLID principles underpin all good design patterns
Understanding trade-offs is critical before applying patterns
Patterns establish shared vocabulary for software teams
anti_patterns: Using patterns without understanding their trade-offs
Global state in Singleton pattern making testing difficult
Complex inheritance hierarchies when Decorator pattern applies

detailed_summary.introduction: Design patterns represent best practices and reusable solutions to common software design problems. Each pattern consists of three elements: the problem it solves, a general solution, and the consequences/trade-offs.

core_concepts.name: Pattern Framework
core_concepts.description: All patterns follow Problem → Solution → Consequences structure

core_concepts.name: SOLID Foundation
core_concepts.description: Five principles that guide pattern design and application

practical_guidance.when_to_use: Apply patterns when they solve real problems in your codebase
practical_guidance.key_principle: Start simple, refactor to patterns when needed

drawbacks: May not apply to specific contexts

key_takeaways: Understand principles behind patterns, not just mechanics
Each pattern has trade-offs to evaluate
Use patterns to solve real problems, avoid over-engineering
Patterns enable better team communication through shared terminology
